pages.title: Petalfall Vernal
pages.text: Springs depart and return; petals fall and bloom again. Legend says the Petalfall Vernal was born of the wilderness's final longing for spring: whenever the first spring flower withers, its form blossoms anew. Petals swirl around it in an unending rain of flowers.

pages.title: Tale
pages.text: Legend tells that the wilderness hoarded a whole spring's worth of longing through the long, bitter winter. When the first spring flower withered beyond recall, that longing finally took root: withered stems stood upright once more, fallen petals flew back against the wind to the branch, and wound about a gentle glow, refusing to scatter. $(br)Since then, wherever a spring flower falls, petals come swirling down in an unending rain. Plants touched by that rain receive the spring's gift of nourishment and renewal — the withered bloom again, wounds slowly heal, just as plants broken by winter always reawaken in the spring breeze.
